belongs_to: Page No. 165, Figure it Out Q4: 'Look at the following rectangles. Which rectangles are similar to each other? You can verify this by measuring the width and height using a scale and comparing their ratios.' (question text on p.23, figure on p.24, reprinted in the solutions part)
description: One picture of FIVE plain rectangles (thin black outline, no fill, no dimensions or numbers written), scattered in different places and orientations, each with one small capital letter centred inside it: A, B, C, D, E. Measured from the picture (short side : long side, about): A - upright (long side vertical), left-lower, about 25 x 77 px, short:long about 1 : 3.1; B - wide rectangle with its long side horizontal, upper left, about 76 x 51 px, ratio about 2 : 3 (1 : 1.5); C - the biggest, centre, tilted so its long side slopes down to the right at about 34 degrees below horizontal, about 87 x 218 px, ratio about 1 : 2.5 (2 : 5); D - top right, tilted so its long side rises to the right at about 18 degrees above horizontal, about 56 x 167 px, ratio about 1 : 3.0; E - smallest tilted one, right of centre, long side sloping down to the right at about 45 degrees, about 29 x 73 px, ratio about 1 : 2.5. So by the picture the similar pairs are A with D (about 1 : 3) and C with E (about 2 : 5); B is not similar to any other. Left to right / top to bottom order on the page: A (lower left), B (upper left), C (large, centre), D (top right), E (right, lower).
unclear: The book prints no side lengths; the ratios above were measured from the page picture and are approximate (A about 1:3.1, D about 1:3.0, C about 1:2.5, E about 1:2.6).
Exact positions and tilt angles are approximate.

belongs_to: Page No. 165, Figure it Out Q6: 'The following figure shows a small portion of a long brick wall with patterns made using coloured bricks ... What is the ratio of grey bricks to coloured bricks?' - wall (a) (question text on p.24, figure on p.25; label '(a)' printed at the left of the wall)
description: Wall (a): label '(a)' at the left. A wall 3 rows high, each row 17 bricks, 51 bricks in all (33 grey, 18 red). Brick colours: light grey and red; the red bricks are the 'coloured' bricks. Rows alternate in a running bond: row 2 (middle) is shifted to the right by about a third of a brick, so it starts a little further right and ends a little beyond the right end of rows 1 and 3. Row 1 (top), left to right (G = grey, R = red): G G R R R G G R R R G G R R R G G (9 R, 8 G). Row 2 (middle, shifted): G G R R G G G R R G G G R R G G G (6 R, 11 G). Row 3 (bottom): G G G R G G G G R G G G G R G G G (3 R, 14 G). The repeating block is 5 bricks wide in every row: row 1 = 2 grey + 3 red, row 2 = 3 grey + 2 red, row 3 = 4 grey + 1 red, i.e. 9 grey and 6 red per block, matching the printed answer 2+3+4 = 9 grey and 3+2+1 = 6 coloured. The red groups are stacked one under another, roughly centred on each other (3 red in row 1, 2 red in row 2, 1 red in row 3), giving an inverted-triangle shape in each block.
unclear: Offset of the middle row measured roughly (about 1/3 brick), not exactly.
Column alignment of the red groups in rows 1-3 read from the picture; all counts verified by pixel analysis along each row.

SMALL RECTANGLE (third room/porch): hangs below the bottom edge of the big rectangle; its left side is the continuation of the inner wall (same vertical line, drawn on down); it is 6 ft wide (label '6 ft' written INSIDE, at its bottom edge) and 9 ft high (label '9 ft' written to the RIGHT of its right side); its top edge is the part of the big rectangle's bottom edge between the inner wall and a point 6 ft to the right.
